summary: Targeted CSV slices of SAM.gov-registered small business government contractors filtered by NAICS code, set-aside type (8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB), and state. SAM.gov is entirely public; subscription tools like GovWin IQ, Bloomberg Government, and SamSearch charge $200-500/month to search it. Subcontractors, IT staffing agencies, and consultants need targeted lists of registered primes to pursue teaming arrangements — they have no cheap one-time option today.

audience.who: Government contracting subcontractors seeking teaming partners, IT staffing agencies targeting federal-contractor clients, management consultants pursuing government market entry, and SaaS vendors who sell tools (proposal software, compliance tools, timekeeping) specifically to federal contractors.

data_wanted: Company name, CAGE code, UEID, primary NAICS codes, small business set-aside certifications (8a/HUBZone/WOSB/SDVOSB/Veteran), physical address, state, POC name and email (from SAM entity registration public data), active registration status, and (where available via USASpending.gov join) total contract dollars awarded.

evidence.source: SAM.gov Contract Data — fully public federal procurement and entity registry, no authentication required for public entity data
evidence.quote: Explore Federal procurement data and contract award records based on awardee, agency, set-asides, and more.

evidence.source: SamSearch — paid subscription aggregating SAM.gov data at $200+/month, proves buyers pay for easier access to this public data
evidence.quote: Most comprehensive platforms like SamSearch and GovWin require subscriptions, though SamSearch offers affordable tiered pricing with significantly broader features than the free SAM.gov interface.

evidence.source: FedBiz Access — government contracting education firm, 2026 guide confirms 24,000+ new SAM.gov contract notices monthly and active small business set-aside landscape
evidence.quote: SAM.gov posts over 24,000 new notices monthly. You can explore opportunities based on NAICS code, set-aside status, location, small business events, and vendor collaboration.

evidence.source: iQuasar — article on using NAICS codes beyond SAM.gov for hidden opportunities, proving active audience researching government contractor prospecting
evidence.quote: Hidden Government Contracting Opportunities: Using NAICS Codes Beyond SAM.gov

willingness_to_pay.signal: GovWin IQ costs $200-500/month. Bloomberg Government costs $500+/month. SamSearch has tiered paid plans. A one-time $49-89 filtered CSV (e.g., '8(a)-certified IT services firms in Virginia with active SAM registration') saves a subcontractor 5+ hours of manual SAM.gov searching and costs less than one month of any subscription tool.

field_coverage.poc_email: 0% — requires SAM.gov entity API key (not public without registration)

harvest.notes: SAM.gov entity API v3 requires a registered API key (free but must register). Used USASpending.gov bulk download API instead — fully public, no auth. poc_email requires SAM.gov entity API key to populate.

first_sale_path.channel: Gumroad listing + Reddit r/govcon, r/usajobs, r/sysadmin (federal IT angle), LinkedIn GovCon groups
first_sale_path.angle: "8(a) IT Contractors — Virginia/DC/Maryland — SAM.gov Active 2026, CSV" — a teaming-ready list of certified small businesses in the DMV federal corridor, for subcontractors and IT staffing firms that want to call primes directly. Angle: 'Skip 5 hours on SAM.gov. Here are the companies. Here is the POC.'
